lunar eclipse.reason: the verdict comes from catalogued eclipses and computed visibility at Babylon in three Delta T trials, with no distance tolerance; the dated corpus has too few testable reports (two parser clauses) for any count gate

moon.reason: the Moon's place on a given day of a lunar month is set mostly by the month itself, so it measures the calendar rather than the year

inner.reason: Venus and Mercury stay within 47 and 28 degrees of the Sun, so their position in a given month repeats on short cycles

last appearance.reason: a last appearance is a visibility event near the Sun, and a visibility model based on elongation alone failed its held-out check
